uc.role.werewolf.name: Werewolf
uc.role.werewolf.desc: As the last Impostor, become the beast in the dark
uc.role.werewolf.intro: As the last Impostor, become the beast in the dark
uc.help.werewolf: An ordinary Impostor - until he is the LAST one. A countdown only runs while the Lights sabotage is active; once it is full he can turn into the beast. For a few seconds nobody can fix the lights, everyone is cut down to a small flashlight (the werewolf keeps full vision, the Lighter keeps his), the wolf runs faster and kills faster, and everyone SEES the wolf. His victims are left inside a ring of blood. Silver is his weakness: in wolf form the first sheriff bullet only wounds him (forced revert, slow, kill cooldown to maximum), the second one kills; in human form silver is lethal right away. Trapper and Saboteur traps wound him too, and the Deputy handcuffs force him back into human shape.
uc.role.hunter.name: Hunter
uc.role.hunter.intro: The beast is the last one left - hunt it down with silver
uc.option.hunter.only_original: Hunter Only From The Original Sheriff
uc.option.hunter.deputy_promotes: Deputy Promotes To Sheriff When The Hunter Rises
uc.option.hunter.hat_costume: Hunter Wears The Monster Hunter Hat
uc.hunter.flavor.crew1: You shiver in fear... the beast is near.
uc.hunter.flavor.crew2: Claw marks by the cams. It is still out there.
uc.hunter.flavor.crew3: Something big moved in the shadows.
uc.hunter.flavor.crew4: The sheriff keeps turning an old, notched silver bolt in his hands.
uc.hunter.flavor.wolf1: You smell silver on the air... you have smelled this hunter before.
uc.hunter.flavor.wolf2: Your old scar burns - the one HIS bolt left, years ago.
uc.hunter.flavor.wolf3: The hunter walks like a man who has done this before.
uc.hunter.flavor.wolf4: One more night. One more kill. Then it is over.
uc.hunter.flavor.hunter1: Your silver bolts hum. The hunt is on - again.
uc.hunter.flavor.hunter2: The old scar on your shoulder aches. You remember its teeth.
uc.hunter.flavor.hunter3: You missed once, long ago. Not tonight.
uc.help.hunter: Not a role you can spawn - the Sheriff's endgame. The moment every Impostor except the Werewolf is dead and the beast is still alive, the Sheriff becomes The Hunter: everyone sees him change EXCEPT the beast itself, which still sees an ordinary crewmate and has to work out who is hunting it. A living Deputy takes over the Sheriff badge, and inside the wolf darkness he sees further than the rest of the crew. His silver kill button follows the Sheriff's rules (the beast and any Impostor die, neutral killers only if the host allows it, an innocent shot kills him instead), and in wolf form the beast still survives the first bolt and dies to the second. In a meeting he may guess: if he was already a Guesser he keeps his full menu, otherwise he gets one guess with only the Werewolf to pick. His costume also protects him: anybody who can see it can no longer guess the Hunter at all (lovers and a jackal's sidekick inherit that knowledge), so only the beast - which cannot see the costume - may still hunt him by guess. The host can switch the costume off entirely; then the promotion stays invisible, the hat becomes an ordinary cosmetic and that protection lapses with it.
uc.role.pelican.name: Pelican
uc.role.pelican.desc: Swallow them all and be the last one standing
uc.role.pelican.intro: Swallow them all and be the last one standing
uc.ui.pelican.hunt_no_meeting: No meetings during the Pelican Hunt
uc.ui.pelican.freed_flash: The Pelican is dead - you are out of the belly!
uc.help.pelican: A solo Neutral who wins as the last one standing. Instead of killing he SWALLOWS: the victim dies, but the body disappears at once and only he sees who he is carrying. The first meeting digests everyone in his belly for good - but if the Pelican dies first, everyone still inside walks back out ALIVE around his corpse, and the vitals station shows them as alive the whole time they are in there. As soon as only he and one other player are alive, the Pelican Hunt starts: a public countdown, and for everyone no meetings, no reports and no venting (abilities and the plain Impostor kill still work). Swallow the last survivor and the Pelican wins alone; let the clock run out and the survivor wins with his own win condition.

uc.help.tesla: Charges exactly two players in a meeting with opposite polarity: one positive, one negative. If the pair then stands too close together, a hidden countdown drains - at zero, both die. Keeping distance pauses the countdown; only the next meeting refills it. Charged players see their own symbol and a warning when it turns dangerous.
uc.help.saboteur: Spends per-round tokens on two abilities: sabotage a task console - the first crewmate to finish it dies - or place invisible floor traps that stun whoever walks into them. The crew can counter by scanning consoles with SEARCH before using them and defusing a found sabotage in the wire-cut minigame.
uc.help.poisoner: Their kills poison the body: whoever reports it gets infected and dies by itself a few meetings later. Only the Medic can save them - they get an antidote button as soon as someone is poisoned and can cure the victim with it. Without the cure, death is only postponed.
uc.help.silencer: Marks a player during the round with a button (cooldown plus a limited budget). The victim is fully mute in the next meeting: they can neither chat nor vote, and the vote does not wait for them. Only in the meeting does a red MUTED tag appear next to their name for everyone - until then the target stays secret.
uc.help.illusionist: Records their own walking path and replays it later at the press of a button: a clone that looks exactly like them walks the recorded route - the perfect fake alibi. The clone is invulnerable: every kill attempt bounces off with a shield flash, just like a Medic shield.
uc.help.maniac: Secretly attaches a bomb to a player. After a while the carrier notices it - for them it ticks audibly faster and faster - and can pass it on by touch; the fuse simply keeps running. When time runs out, the bomb explodes and kills everyone in range (who exactly is configurable).
uc.help.shade: Their victims' bodies vanish the moment they are killed. They only become visible - and reportable - again once another player walks close enough to the kill spot. Until then the crew has no trace at all: no body, no report, no way to know whether someone is just busy or long dead.
uc.help.manipulator: At the press of a button the ship's security lies to EVERYONE: the admin table shows a fabricated but believable player distribution (the same one for every client), and vitals shows dead players as alive again. The deception is deliberately subtle - no static, no flicker - and ends by itself after a configurable duration.
uc.help.auditor: Every task a LIVING crewmate finishes also lands in the Auditor's own task list. If he goes and does that task himself, it is reset to open for exactly that crewmate - the task bar really drops. His queue only holds a few tasks at a time (further completions are lost), each entry has its own lifetime, and a task becomes untouchable once its owner is known to be dead. His kill cooldown scales with the number of reverts: punishingly slow at the start, dangerous once he has put in the work.
uc.help.siphoner: A passive crewmate with no buttons at all: standing close enough to an Impostor drains their kill power - the Impostor's kill cooldown keeps getting pushed back as long as the Siphoner stays in range. The Impostor only notices that their kill button never seems to finish charging.
uc.help.witness: If they are the only living crewmate to directly witness a kill, they take note of the murderer: that player's name glows red for them. If the Witness survives to the next meeting, a few random players receive an anonymous note naming the killer. If they die first and their body is reported, the note appears in chat for everyone.
uc.help.scout: Activates scout mode at the press of a button for a short time: they become much faster, nearly transparent, and light sabotage does not limit their vision meanwhile. Duration, speed bonus and transparency are configurable. Ideal for sweeping dark routes, finding bodies or secretly witnessing a kill.
uc.help.beacon: Light sabotage never affects them - the Beacon always keeps full vision. Even better: every crewmate standing close enough with a clear line of sight to the Beacon shares that full vision for as long as they stay in range. During light sabotage the Beacon becomes a walking lighthouse for the whole crew.
uc.help.bug: Has no abilities whatsoever - they just have to survive to the end. When a team wins (crew, impostors or the Jackal team), a still-living Bug snatches that victory and wins alone instead. Solo wins of other neutrals (like the Jester) are never stolen. If the Bug dies, their game is simply over.
uc.help.follower: Starts without a fixed team. The first player to die - by kill or ejection - decides their fate: the Follower takes over that player's entire role with team, abilities and win condition, and carries on in their place. If an Impostor dies first, the Follower becomes an Impostor themselves.
uc.help.copycat: Whenever anyone in the game uses a copyable ability - camouflage, morphing, shield, a shot or venting - the Copycat learns it and gets its own button for it. Slots are limited; the oldest ability is dropped. They win alongside the winning team if they are alive at the end and have used enough abilities.
uc.help.collector: Relics are hidden across the map, clearly visible only to the Collector. They must stand at a relic for a few seconds and channel - moving cancels, and anyone close enough hears a soft glitter. Collecting enough relics wins the game alone: instantly or at the next team win, depending on the option - as long as they live.
uc.help.poltergeist: Not a starting role: the first player to die rises as the Poltergeist and keeps haunting for their original team. A slowly regenerating energy pool pays for four powers: slamming doors shut, hexing players (speed, blind or night vision), acting as one hand at the reactor, or briefly appearing as a copy of a living player.

tor.help.jester: The Jester has no tasks and wins solo by getting voted out during a meeting. They should act suspicious enough to get exiled without being mistaken for an Impostor. Depending on settings, the Jester can have Impostor vision or lose the ability to call emergency meetings.
tor.help.mayor: The Mayor's vote counts twice, helping sway meeting outcomes toward the crew. They can always call a meeting even if the maximum number of meetings has been reached, and may see vote colors after enough tasks are done. A portable meeting button can also be granted depending on the settings.
tor.help.portalmaker: The Portalmaker places two linked portals on the map that become usable by everyone after the next meeting. They can optionally teleport to their own portals from anywhere and receive chat log information about who used them. Ghosts can use the portals too but do not block living players or generate log entries.
tor.help.engineer: The Engineer can fix a limited number of sabotages from anywhere on the map and is able to use vents. If they hide inside a vent, Impostors (and the Jackal team, depending on settings) can be shown a highlighted outline warning them, and the Impostor kill button activates next to that vent.
tor.help.sheriff: The Sheriff can shoot and kill Impostors, and Neutral roles if enabled, but dies instead if they shoot a Crewmate. If the Sheriff shoots a player protected by the Medic's shield, both the Sheriff and the shielded player survive unharmed, and shooting a growing Mini has no effect at all.
tor.help.deputy: The Deputy can handcuff players, disabling their kill, ability, vent, and report actions for a duration once the cuffs become visible. The Deputy cannot exist in a game without the Sheriff, and depending on settings may be promoted to Sheriff if the Sheriff dies.
tor.help.lighter: The Lighter has a special flashlight-like vision that can be moved around, differing from everyone else's vision depending on whether the lights are on or off. Their vision cone strength in both states can be configured in the settings.
tor.help.godfather: The Godfather is part of the three-member Mafia team alongside the Mafioso and Janitor, and otherwise plays and kills like a normal Impostor. The Mafia can only spawn if three Impostors are active in the game.
tor.help.mafioso: The Mafioso is a Mafia Impostor who cannot kill until the Godfather has died, after which they take over killing duties. They are part of the three-member Mafia team together with the Godfather and Janitor, which requires three active Impostors to spawn.
tor.help.janitor: The Janitor is a Mafia Impostor who cannot kill, but can instead hide dead bodies to cover the team's tracks. They are part of the three-member Mafia team with the Godfather and Mafioso, which needs three active Impostors to appear.
tor.help.morphling: The Morphling can scan a player's appearance and later take on that look for a set duration, including their footprint color and admin table entry. They shrink to Mini size if copying the Mini's look, but still appear red to other Impostors and remain trackable by the Tracker.
tor.help.camouflager: The Camouflager can trigger a camouflage mode that hides everyone's name, pet, and hat and gives all players the same color for a set duration. Footprints turn gray and shields become invisible while camouflage is active, but Tracker arrows still function normally.
tor.help.vampire: The Vampire bites a player, who then dies after a configurable delay, or performs a normal kill if the target is near a garlic, which any player can place. A bitten player who is still alive when a meeting starts dies as the meeting begins, and the Vampire cannot coexist with the Warlock in the same game.
tor.help.eraser: The Eraser can target any player to erase their role, which is applied right before the next exile even if the Eraser or target has died in the meantime. By default the Spy and other Impostors are immune unless the settings allow erasing them, and each erase increases the Eraser's cooldown.
tor.help.trickster: The Trickster places three jack-in-the-boxes that are invisible to others until all three are set, after which they become a private vent network for the Trickster and are revealed to everyone else. Once the vent network exists, the Trickster gains a Lights Out ability that blinds non-Impostors without triggering the usual sabotage warning.
tor.help.cleaner: The Cleaner can remove dead bodies from the map, sharing a cooldown with their kill ability so they cannot immediately clean their own kills. The Cleaner cannot appear in the same game as the Vulture.
tor.help.warlock: The Warlock secretly curses a player; if that player stands next to anyone, the Warlock can kill that nearby target from any distance. Using the curse to kill lifts the curse and roots the Warlock in place for a while, though normal kills are also possible on a shared cooldown and do not lift an active curse.
tor.help.bountyHunter: The Bounty Hunter receives a secret bounty target that changes after each meeting or after a set time. Killing the current bounty greatly reduces the kill cooldown, while killing anyone else increases it, and an arrow can optionally point toward the target, who will never be an Impostor, Spy, or the Bounty Hunter's own Lover.
tor.help.detective: The Detective can see the footprints players leave behind, and when reporting a corpse receives clues about the killer's identity based on how quickly the body was found. Footprints change color to match a Morphling or Camouflager in effect, but are never left by players inside vents.
tor.help.timeMaster: The Time Master can activate a time shield that rewinds a failed murder attempt against them for a set duration, without resetting the killer's own cooldown. The Time Master themself is unaffected by the rewind, though a Medic shield on them will prevent the rewind from triggering at all.
tor.help.medic: The Medic can shield one player per game, making them unkillable by normal murder attempts, with the shield shown as brackets around the name in meetings. A shielded player can still be voted out even if they are an Impostor, and the Sheriff neither dies nor performs a kill when targeting a shielded player. The Medic can optionally see when someone attempts to murder their shielded target.
tor.help.swapper: During meetings the Swapper can exchange the votes of two players, so votes for one go to the other instead. In exchange for this strength, the Swapper cannot call emergency meetings or fix sabotages, and has a limited number of swap charges that recharge as tasks are completed.
tor.help.seer: The Seer can see the fading souls of players who died a round earlier and can receive a screen flash whenever anyone dies anywhere on the map, depending on which abilities are enabled. Both effects give passive information about recent deaths without revealing exact details.
tor.help.hacker: Activating Hacker mode lets the Hacker see extra details on the admin table (player colors) and vitals (time since death) for a limited duration, using charges that recharge via completed tasks. The Hacker cannot move while accessing these mobile gadgets, and sees color changes reflecting an active Morphling or Camouflager.
tor.help.tracker: The Tracker selects a player to track, with an arrow pointing to their last known position that updates periodically, and depending on settings can track a new person each meeting or the same one all game. An optional second ability lets the Tracker locate all corpses on the map for a while, even ones that were cleaned or eaten by the Vulture.
tor.help.snitch: Once the Snitch finishes all their tasks, they receive the last known location of every killer in chat at the start of each meeting. When the Snitch is close to finishing, a configurable number of tasks remaining, evil players are warned in advance that a Snitch is active in the game.
tor.help.jackal: The Jackal leads their own team and wins by eliminating everyone else, having no tasks but the ability to kill Impostors, Crewmates, and Neutrals alike. They can convert another player into their Sidekick, who joins the Jackal's team and loses their previous role, and the Jackal can still be killed by the Sheriff.
tor.help.sidekick: The Sidekick is created mid-game by the Jackal's ability and joins them in trying to eliminate every other player, losing their previous role and tasks in the process. If the Jackal dies, the Sidekick may be promoted to Jackal themselves, depending on the settings, and can still be killed by the Sheriff.
tor.help.spy: The Spy is a Crewmate with no special ability who appears as an extra Impostor to the actual Impostors, who cannot tell them apart from their real teammates. Depending on the settings, Impostors either cannot kill the Spy at all, or risk mistakenly killing their own partner instead.
tor.help.securityGuard: The Security Guard spends a limited pool of screws to either place new cameras or seal off vents, with both actions taking effect after the next meeting. Sealed vents can no longer be entered or exited, and after using all their screws the Security Guard can access mobile cameras remotely, though they cannot move while doing so.
tor.help.arsonist: The Arsonist has no tasks and wins alone by dousing every living player one at a time and then igniting them all at once. Walking away from an in-progress dousing resets that cooldown to zero, so the Arsonist must stay close to their target until it completes.
tor.help.goodGuesser: The Nice Guesser is a Crewmate (or other team, depending on settings) who can shoot another player during a meeting by correctly guessing their exact role, killing them; guessing wrong kills the Guesser instead. Votes are returned if a shot lands, and a guess only counts as correct if the target's team and lack of special role match exactly.
tor.help.badGuesser: The Evil Guesser is an Impostor variant of the Guesser who can shoot another player during a meeting by correctly guessing their role, killing them, but dies themself on a wrong guess. Depending on settings they may or may not be allowed to guess the Spy, and a shielded player can be immune to the guess entirely.
tor.help.vulture: The Vulture has no tasks and wins alone by eating a set number of corpses, optionally getting an arrow pointing to each new body as it appears. The Vulture cannot appear in the same game as the Cleaner.
tor.help.medium: The Medium can question the fading souls of players who died the previous round, receiving random hints in chat about the victim or their killer, preferring role-specific hints first. Souls disappear after one round and, depending on settings, may only be questioned a single time before vanishing.
tor.help.trapper: The Trapper sets hidden traps that stun anyone who steps in them and reveal information about the trapped player, such as their name, role, or good/evil alignment, once enough triggers have accumulated. Traps have a limited number of charges that recharge through completed tasks, and the Trapper cannot be caught in their own traps.
tor.help.lawyer: The Lawyer has a secret client, usually an Impostor or Jackal (or Jester, if enabled), and wins together with that client's team if the client survives and wins. If their client dies first, the Lawyer instead becomes the Pursuer with a new win condition, and if the client is voted out, the Lawyer dies alongside them.
tor.help.prosecutor: The Prosecutor is a variant of the Lawyer whose secret client is a Crewmate, and wins by getting that client voted out. If the client is sidekicked, the Prosecutor instead becomes their Lawyer and must protect them, and if the client dies some other way, the Prosecutor becomes the Pursuer instead.
tor.help.pursuer: The Pursuer wins by surviving to the end of a Crewmate victory, using a Blank ability that makes a killer's next attempt, including the Sheriff's, miss without triggering shields like the Medic or Time Master. Former Lawyers and Prosecutors become the Pursuer once their client dies, and the Pursuer's tasks only count toward the crew's task win after that promotion.
tor.help.impostor: The Impostor's goal is to sabotage the ship and secretly kill Crewmates until the Impostors equal or outnumber the remaining crew. Impostors can vent, trigger sabotages, and see who their fellow Impostors are.
tor.help.crewmate: The Crewmate has no special ability and wins by completing all assigned tasks or by voting out every Impostor and hostile Neutral. Crewmates rely on teamwork, observation, and the special roles among them to find the Impostors.
tor.help.witch: The Witch can cast a spell on a player that marks them to die right after the next meeting ends, with shields and blanks checked both when the spell is cast and when it resolves. If the Witch dies or is guessed before the meeting concludes, spelled players are still highlighted but survive, and voting the Witch out can optionally save every spelled target.
tor.help.ninja: The Ninja marks a player and can later use their ability again to teleport to that player's position and kill them instantly, leaving behind a fading trace at both the mark and kill locations. Depending on settings the Ninja may briefly turn invisible after a marked kill, but only a meeting resets the mark, not a normal kill.
tor.help.thief: The Thief must kill another killer, such as an Impostor, Jackal, Sidekick, or, if enabled, the Sheriff, to gain a win condition, taking over that role and joining its team upon success. If the Thief instead kills a non-killing Crewmate or Neutral, they die just like a Sheriff who shoots the wrong target.
tor.help.bomber: The Bomber can plant bombs that explode after a delay, killing and scattering nearby Crewmates, in addition to performing normal kills. Crewmates can defuse a planted bomb in time depending on the settings, and the bomb will not harm shielded players or an ungrown Mini, though it can kill the Bomber and their own teammates too.
tor.help.yoyo: The Yo-Yo marks a location and can blink there instantly, then automatically blinks back to their starting point after a limited window of time to act. Each blink leaves behind a faint, hard-to-see silhouette, and the Yo-Yo may also get access to a mobile admin table depending on the settings.
tor.help.hunter: In the Hide 'n Seek gamemode, the Hunter plays the Impostor role and must catch and kill every Hunted player before time runs out. Movement is disabled for a few seconds at the round's start, and Hunters can use ability charges such as revealing arrows toward Hunted players, a mobile admin table, and a temporary vision boost.
tor.help.hunted: In the Hide 'n Seek gamemode, the Hunted plays the Crewmate role and must evade the Hunters until the round timer runs out or all crew tasks are completed. The Hunted can activate a Time Master-like shield to survive a kill attempt, at the cost of triggering a rewind for the Hunter instead of themselves.
tor.help.prop: In the PropHunt gamemode, the Prop plays the Crewmate role and can disguise as an object on the map to hide from the Hunters, while using invisibility and speed boosts to survive until time runs out. If a Prop is found and killed, they may either join the Hunter team or die outright, depending on the settings.
tor.help.bloody: If a player with the Bloody modifier is killed, their killer leaves behind a colored trail matching the victim for a set number of seconds. Any Impostor, Neutral, or Crewmate role can carry this modifier, and it can appear on more than one player per game.
tor.help.antiTeleport: A player with the Anti Teleport modifier is not teleported to the meeting table when a body is reported or an emergency meeting is called, instead starting the round from where the previous one ended. Any Impostor, Neutral, or Crewmate role can carry this modifier.
tor.help.tiebreaker: If a vote ends in a tie, the player with the Tiebreaker modifier secretly casts an extra vote that decides the outcome, though everyone learns afterward whether the Tiebreaker was involved. Only one player per game can hold this modifier, and it can be applied to any Impostor, Neutral, or Crewmate role.
tor.help.bait: A player with the Bait modifier forces their killer to automatically self-report the body, optionally after a configurable delay. More than one Bait can exist per game, and it can be applied to any Impostor, Neutral, or Crewmate role, though a Sheriff who misfires while carrying Bait will not self-report.
tor.help.sunglasses: The Sunglasses modifier reduces a Crewmate's vision by a configurable percentage, and this reduction also applies when the lights are sabotaged. Only Crewmates can carry this modifier, and it is lost if the player is later sidekicked.
tor.help.lover: Two Lovers are secretly linked and win together if both survive to the end of the game, regardless of their individual roles, and can also achieve a solo win if one of them is a killer. If one Lover dies, the other may automatically suicide depending on the settings, and an optional private chat lets them communicate.
tor.help.mini: The Mini modifier shrinks the player's character and makes them immune to being killed until they finish growing up, though they can still be voted out. Impostor Minis have a doubled kill cooldown while growing and a shortened one once grown, while a Crewmate or Jester Mini being voted out before growing up ends badly for their team.
tor.help.vip: The VIP modifier makes everyone see a screen flash, similar to the Seer's death flash, whenever that player dies, optionally colored to show which team they belonged to. It can be applied to Impostor, Jackal, or Crewmate roles.
tor.help.invert: The Invert modifier reverses a player's movement controls, whether they use keyboard or mouse input. It can be applied to any Impostor, Neutral, or Crewmate role.
tor.help.chameleon: The Chameleon modifier makes a player partially or fully invisible after standing still for a few seconds, though using abilities does not break the invisibility, only moving does. It can be applied to any Impostor, Neutral, or Crewmate role.
tor.help.armored: The Armored modifier protects its holder from the very first murder attempt that would have killed them during a round, breaking with a visible animation for the attacker. It does not protect against votes or guesses, and only one player per round can be Armored.
tor.help.shifter: The Shifter can choose another player to swap roles with at the end of the next meeting; swapping with a fellow Crewmate exchanges their roles, but attempting to swap with an Impostor or Neutral instead makes the Shifter secretly suicide with no body left behind. Only a Crewmate role can carry the Shifter modifier, and the shift resolves before the Eraser's effect if both occur in the same meeting.

uc.help.gambler: A crew modifier: he bets on what the round will do - who gets voted out, how many votes someone gets, whether a kill happens, whether a target really finishes tasks. Never on himself. Every bet is settled INSIDE a meeting, so a win never tells him anything early. The tier is the stake: the small ones only change his own speed, the middle ones give or take one of his own tasks, and the top ones stretch or shorten every impostor's kill cooldown - which the impostors are told about, but not who did it.
